modern: Any one activity, whatever it may be, when it has ceased at its proper time, suffers no evil because it has ceased; nor does he who has done this act suffer any evil for this reason, that the act has ceased. In the same way, then, the whole, which consists of all the acts, which is our life, if it ceases at its proper time, suffers no evil for this reason, that it has ceased; nor has he who has ended this series at the proper time been badly treated. But the proper time and the limit are fixed by nature: sometimes, as in old age, by the particular nature of man, but always by the universal nature, through the change of whose parts the whole universe stays ever young and perfect. And everything which is useful to the universal is always good and in season. Therefore the ending of life for every man is no evil, because it is not shameful, since it is both independent of the will and not opposed to the general interest; but it is good, since it is timely, and profitable to and in harmony with the universal. For in this way too he is moved by the Deity who is moved in the same way as the Deity, and moved towards the same thing in his mind.
